name: effects-external-ref-and-script
story: An end-of-programme sponsor card exported from Sketch, then hand-edited: the designer swapped the embedded badge for a CDN link so it would "always show the current sponsor", and pasted in a loader snippet from a tutorial to fade that badge up.
idioms: width="1920px" height="1080px" with px UNITS on the root, alongside viewBox and version="1.1"
<title>Sponsor card</title> and <desc>Created with Sketch.</desc> as the first two children
the artboard wrapped in <g id="Sponsor-card" stroke="none" stroke-width="1" fill="none" fill-rule="evenodd">, Sketch's fixed reset group
explicit closing tags on empty elements (<rect ...></rect>, <image ...></image>) rather than self-closing
text as <text id=..><tspan x=.. y=..>…</tspan></text> with the baseline on the tspan
font-family="Archivo-Bold, Archivo" - PostScript face first, family second - with font-weight repeated alongside
the hand edit: xlink:href="https://example.com/badge.png" on an <image> that was an embedded data: URI when Sketch wrote it
the hand edit: a trailing <script type="text/javascript"><![CDATA[ … ]]></script> holding an IIFE that reaches getElementById and window.addEventListener
whyThisMatters: This is the file that must be made safe without being refused: the https image and the script have to come out and be REPORTED - a graphic that reaches the network dies on a playout machine with no internet, and an imported script runs inside preview, exports and shared templates - while the card's two live text lines still have to arrive as fields, so a sanitizer that throws the whole file away is as wrong as one that keeps the script.
